ADMISSION NOTE — General Internal Medicine
Date of admission: 18 October 2026, 21:40

Patient: Morgan FAKE-Ellison · DOB: 9 February 1952 (74 years) · Health card: 9999990452 (FAKE)
Family physician: Dr. Henrietta Fakeham (FAKE), Maple Test Family Health Team
Admitting physician: Dr. Ian Sampleton (FAKE), Internal Medicine

Reason for admission
Fever, confusion and burning on passing urine for two days. The patient's daughter, who lives with them, found them confused and unsteady this evening and called an ambulance.

History of present illness
Mx. FAKE-Ellison was well until three days ago, when they began to pass urine more often, with burning and a feeling of not emptying fully. Two days ago they had shivers and a temperature of 38.9 °C at home. They have eaten and drunk little since. Today they were drowsy and did not recognize the date. There was no fall, no head injury, no cough, no chest pain and no diarrhea.

Past medical history
- Type 2 diabetes for 18 years, on metformin and gliclazide. Last HbA1c 7.6% in August 2026.
- Hypertension, on amlodipine and perindopril.
- Chronic kidney disease stage 3a; usual creatinine about 110 µmol/L.
- Mild cognitive impairment noted in 2025; lives at home with their daughter and manages their own pills with a weekly dosette.
- Urinary urge incontinence since a hysterectomy in 1998.
- Osteoporosis, on weekly alendronate.

Medications before admission
- Metformin 1000 mg twice daily
- Gliclazide MR 60 mg once daily
- Amlodipine 10 mg once daily
- Perindopril 4 mg once daily
- Alendronate 70 mg once weekly
- Vitamin D 1000 units daily

Allergies: sulfa drugs (hives).

Examination
Temperature 39.2 °C, heart rate 112, blood pressure 96/58, respiratory rate 22, oxygen saturation 95% on room air. Drowsy but rousable, oriented to person only. Dry mouth. Tender over the right flank. Chest clear. Heart sounds normal. No neck stiffness. No focal weakness.

Initial results
White cells 18.4 ×10⁹/L, CRP 212 mg/L, lactate 3.1 mmol/L, creatinine 198 µmol/L, urea 14.2 mmol/L, potassium 5.1 mmol/L, glucose 16.8 mmol/L. Urine dipstick: leukocytes and nitrites positive. Blood and urine cultures sent before antibiotics.

Assessment
Sepsis from a right-sided kidney infection (pyelonephritis), with acute kidney injury on chronic kidney disease and delirium from the infection.

Plan
- IV fluids: 1 litre of Ringer's lactate now, then by blood pressure and urine output.
- Ceftriaxone 2 g IV once daily (sulfa allergy noted; no cephalosporin allergy).
- Hold metformin, perindopril and amlodipine while blood pressure is low and kidney function is poor.
- Hold gliclazide; insulin sliding scale with glucose checks before meals and at bedtime.
- Delirium care: daughter may stay, lights and clock in the room, glasses and hearing aid on.
- Ultrasound of the kidneys tomorrow to look for a blockage or abscess.

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD — 18 October 2026
Arrival 19:55 by ambulance. Triage level 2.

Paramedic report: found by daughter sitting on the edge of the bed, confused, warm to touch. Blood glucose on scene 17.1 mmol/L. No seizure activity. Given 500 mL of normal saline on the way.

Emergency physician assessment (Dr. Kai FAKE-Brennan): 74-year-old with diabetes and chronic kidney disease, three days of urinary symptoms, two days of fever, and new confusion today. Looks unwell. Temperature 39.2 °C, heart rate 112, blood pressure 96/58 after the first fluid bolus, oxygen saturation 95% on room air. Confusion Assessment Method positive for delirium. Right costovertebral angle tenderness. No meningism. Capillary refill 3 seconds.

Investigations ordered: complete blood count, electrolytes, creatinine, glucose, lactate, venous blood gas, blood cultures ×2, urinalysis and urine culture, ECG, chest X-ray.
ECG: sinus tachycardia at 110, no acute ischemic changes. Chest X-ray: no pneumonia, no fluid in the lungs.
Venous blood gas: pH 7.31, bicarbonate 18 mmol/L, lactate 3.1 mmol/L.

Treatment in the emergency department: Ringer's lactate 1 litre over 30 minutes, then a second litre over 1 hour. Ceftriaxone 2 g IV given at 20:50, within one hour of arrival. Acetaminophen 1 g by mouth for fever. Blood pressure improved to 104/62 after fluids.
Disposition: admitted to General Internal Medicine under Dr. Sampleton.

NURSING ADMISSION ASSESSMENT — 18 October 2026, 23:10

Lives with: daughter (Riley FAKE-Ellison), in a two-storey house; bedroom upstairs, bathroom on both floors.
Mobility before admission: independent indoors with a cane; uses a walker outdoors. One fall in the past year, without injury.
Activities of daily living: independent with washing and dressing; the daughter helps with shopping and fills the weekly dosette.
Continence: urge incontinence, uses pads at night.
Skin: intact; Braden score 15 (moderate risk). Heels offloaded.
Nutrition: usual weight 64 kg; weighed today 61.5 kg. Poor intake for 3 days. Dietitian referral made.
Cognition: confused tonight; usually oriented. Wears glasses and a hearing aid in the left ear.
Belongings: glasses, hearing aid, dentures (upper plate), cane.
Advance care planning: full treatment; the daughter is the substitute decision-maker.
Falls risk: high (confusion, urgency, cane). Bed in low position, alarm on, hourly rounding.

PROGRESS NOTE — 19 October 2026 (Hospital day 1)
Internal Medicine, Dr. Ian Sampleton (FAKE)

Subjective
Still feverish overnight, 38.6 °C. Drowsy in the morning, more alert by noon. Took small sips of fluid. Urine output 25 mL per hour after 2.5 litres of fluid.

Objective
Blood pressure 108/64, heart rate 98. Right flank still tender.

Results
Creatinine 186 µmol/L, CRP 240 mg/L, lactate 1.8 mmol/L.

Assessment and plan
Kidney ultrasound: no blockage, no abscess; the right kidney is swollen, which fits infection. Continue ceftriaxone. Continue IV fluids at 100 mL per hour.

Nursing summary, 19 October 2026
Vital signs every 4 hours. Fluid balance charted. Pressure areas checked twice; skin intact. Falls risk high: bed alarm on, call bell within reach, non-slip socks. The daughter visited in the afternoon and was updated at the bedside. Medications given as prescribed; no missed doses.

PHYSIOTHERAPY AND OCCUPATIONAL THERAPY NOTES

Physiotherapy, 20 October 2026: assessed in bed and at the bedside. Strength reduced in both legs (4/5). Sit-to-stand with one person assisting. Walked 10 metres with a walker and one person. Plan: walk three times a day with staff.
Physiotherapy, 23 October 2026: walked 60 metres with a walker, supervision only. Climbed 6 stairs with a rail and supervision. Safe for home with a walker, with someone present for the first week.
Physiotherapy, 27 October 2026: walked 80 metres with a walker independently after the diarrhea settled. Climbed a full flight of stairs with the rail. Home exercise sheet given.
Occupational therapy, 26 October 2026: washing and dressing with set-up only. Recommends a raised toilet seat and a shower chair; the daughter will buy them. A community home safety visit has been requested.
Dietitian, 21 October 2026: intake about half of meals. Oral nutrition supplement twice daily while in hospital. Weight at discharge 60.8 kg (usual 64 kg).

CONSULTATIONS AND RESULTS

Geriatric medicine consultation — 22 October 2026 (Dr. Lena FAKE-Morrow)
Reason: delirium in a patient with mild cognitive impairment.
The confusion came on with the infection and is clearing as it is treated. Before this illness the patient managed their own medicines with a weekly dosette and did their own shopping with help. Montreal Cognitive Assessment today 22/30, similar to 2025. No new medicines that worsen confusion. Recommendations: continue delirium care, avoid sedatives, home with daughter when medically ready, community occupational therapy home safety visit, and a follow-up memory clinic visit as already planned for January 2027.

Pharmacy medication review — 23 October 2026
The patient takes medicines from a weekly dosette filled by the daughter. A new dosette list was prepared with the changes at discharge. Alendronate is taken on Sunday mornings with water, 30 minutes before food. Sulfa allergy documented; trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole must not be used.

SOCIAL WORK AND INFECTION PREVENTION NOTES

Social work, 26 October 2026 (Alex FAKE-Duval): met with the patient and daughter. The daughter works full time and will take one week of leave. A neighbour can check in at lunchtime in the second week. Home care nursing referral made for a medication check and a wellness visit twice a week for 2 weeks. The patient wants to return home and has capacity for this decision. Caregiver stress discussed; the daughter was given the community caregiver support line.

Infection prevention and control, 25 October 2026: confirmed C. difficile infection. Contact precautions until 48 hours after the diarrhea stops. Single room with its own bathroom. Visitors to wash hands with soap and water on leaving the room. At home: wash hands with soap and water after the toilet and before food; clean the toilet and bathroom taps with a bleach-based cleaner daily until 2 days after the diarrhea stops; wash soiled laundry separately on a hot cycle. No need to stay away from other people once the diarrhea has stopped, but hand washing should continue.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 18 October 2026 · Discharged 28 October 2026 · Internal Medicine, Dr. Ian Sampleton (FAKE)

Diagnoses
1. Sepsis from right pyelonephritis (kidney infection) with Escherichia coli in the blood, treated.
2. Acute kidney injury on chronic kidney disease stage 3a; creatinine back to 115 µmol/L at discharge (usual about 110).
3. Clostridioides difficile diarrhea after antibiotics, improving on oral vancomycin.
4. Delirium caused by the infection, resolved.
5. Type 2 diabetes, hypertension, mild cognitive impairment, osteoporosis.

Medications at discharge
- Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg by mouth twice daily until 31 October 2026, then stop. NEW
- Vancomycin 125 mg by mouth four times daily until 3 November 2026, then stop. NEW
- Metformin 500 mg twice daily. CHANGED (was 1000 mg twice daily)
- Gliclazide MR 30 mg once daily. CHANGED (was 60 mg)
- Amlodipine 5 mg once daily. CHANGED (was 10 mg)
- Perindopril: ON HOLD until the family physician reviews the kidney blood test.
- Alendronate 70 mg once weekly. Continued.
- Vitamin D 1000 units daily. Continued.

Instructions to the patient and family
- Finish both antibiotics, even when you feel well. The last dose of amoxicillin-clavulanate is on the evening of 31 October 2026, and the last dose of vancomycin on 3 November 2026.
- Wash your hands with soap and water after using the toilet and before eating; alcohol gel does not kill the diarrhea germ. Clean the toilet with a bleach cleaner every day until the diarrhea has stopped for 2 days.
- Do not take loperamide (Imodium) for the diarrhea.
- Do not restart perindopril until your family physician tells you to.
- Drink about 6 to 8 glasses of fluid a day unless told otherwise.
- Check your blood sugar once a day before breakfast and write it down; bring the list to your family physician.
- Come back to the emergency department if you have a fever over 38 °C, shivers, new confusion, pain in your side, if you pass very little urine, or if you have more than 6 loose stools a day or blood in the stool.

Follow-up
- Blood test (creatinine, potassium, CBC) in 1 week, around 4 November 2026. A requisition was given.
- Family physician, Dr. Fakeham, within 10 days to review the blood test, the blood pressure and the perindopril.
- Community occupational therapy home safety visit: referral sent.
- Memory clinic in January 2027, as already booked.
